text:
Maria S: heads-up, deploy to rate-exemptions-service (migrations/v2) is causing a large spike in 429s for a subset of long-running sessions. Noticing missing exemptions for reserved-token customers. linking logs: https://logs.redwood.example/tx/XYZ123 :facepalm:

IncidentBot: ALERT: rate-exemptions-migration failure detected. triggered by svc-rate-limiter / memory pressure / config mismatch. Priority: P1. Pager sent to #eng-oncall.

Aj K: @ops-oncall please take. Are we seeing widespread customer impact or limited to a single shard?

ops-oncall: taking it. seeing ~11% 429 rate across api-gateway-prod for token-type=reserved since 09:17 UTC. Error-rate by region: us-west-2 13%, eu-west-1 4%.

Sanjay R: can you paste the failing config diff? my hunch is the exemptions index failed to create and new logic treats missing index as deny.

Maria S: paste of the migration diff (trimmed):
```
- exemptions_index = "ex_v1"
+ exemptions_index = "ex_v2"
+ if not_exists(exemptions_index): default_allow = false
```
looks like v2 defaults to deny when index absent. that would immediately stop exemptions for older tokens.

Evan L: deploy-bot: deploy https://deploys.redwood.example/commit/af34 -> rate-exemptions-service v2 (canary 3/10). Canary health flipped to FAIL at 09:18:22.

Latia M: customer-success reporting several paid customers seeing repeated auth throttles, e.g., ACME corp (redacted) on us-west. they report 5-10% failed calls. cs has open ticket and is requesting ETA.

Aj K: immediate mitigations: 1) flip feature-flag to revert migration v2, 2) if that doesn't help, roll back the entire service to previous docker image, 3) temporarily widen rate thresholds for reserved-token class. Which is fastest?

ops-oncall: flip flag is fastest. flag name: `exemptions.migration_v2.enabled` set to `false` in config-store. running: 
```
$ curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://cfg.redwood.example/flags/exemptions.migration_v2.enabled -d '{"value": false}'
{"status":"ok","applied_at":"2026-03-14T09:21:03Z"}
```

IncidentBot: ACTION: feature flag flip executed by ops-oncall at 2026-03-14T09:21:03Z. Auto-check scheduled in 60s.

ops-oncall: immediate metrics after flip: 1min window shows 429 down from 11% -> 6% and continuing to trend down. initiating canary hold and further verification.

Sanjay R: good. still want to followup with a rollback of the migration code path — even though flag flip mitigates, we need a root cause. Recording command used to check index existence: 
```
$ curl -s https://kv.redwood.example/exemptions/indices | jq .
[
  "ex_v1",
  "legacy_ex"
]
```
We can see ex_v2 not present; migration assumed eventual consistency but code path didn't handle missing index.

Maria S: customer impact estimate: approx 120M tokens/hour affected, primarily telemetry + enterprise reserved customers. CS estimates 9 customers with noticeable failures (two escalations). No financial outages reported yet, but degraded UX.

Evan L: can we add a quick allowance rule in the rate-limiter to treat missing-index as allow for 30m while we reconcile? That would be a short-term safe config.

Aj K: authorized. ops-oncall, apply temporary rule: `allow_if_index_missing = true` for reserved-token class. Show command.

ops-oncall: applied via runtime-config push at 09:26:10Z. verification: 429s back to baseline ~0.5% in 5m.

IncidentBot: NOTE: mitigation bundle applied: [flag flip, runtime allow rule]. oncall: Sanjay R. next check-in in 30m.

Latia M: looped in CS to notify impacted customers: sent initial message with ETA ~30-60m. cs ticket numbers: CS-5231, CS-5232.

Sanjay R: brief postmortem notes to capture root cause: migration v2 introduced a non-backwards-compatible default (`default_allow=false`) when the expected new index isn't present. The deployment assumed the index would be created ahead of traffic; it wasn't, causing a deny-by-default for exemptions. Also missing integration test for index absence.

Aj K: action items assigned:
- Maria S: open postmortem + timeline (due EOD)
- Evan L: add integration test that simulates absent indices (PR queued)
- Ops-oncall (Sanjay): schedule a follow-up to reconcile indices and run migration with canary off-peak
- Product: review rollout checklist to include index provisioning and sanity checks

Maria S: quick timeline for the thread:
- 09:17 UTC: degraded 429s start after canary flip
- 09:18 UTC: canary health FAIL reported
- 09:21 UTC: feature-flag flip executed (mitigation 1)
- 09:26 UTC: runtime allow-rule applied (mitigation 2)
- 09:33 UTC: 429s returned to baseline, CS notified

Evan L: adding logs we used for verification (sanitized):
```
REQUEST /v1/generate 200 ok - token_type=on_demand
REQUEST /v1/generate 429 throttle - token_type=reserved
REQUEST /v1/generate 200 ok - token_type=reserved  <-- post-mitigation
```

Latia M: CS follow-up: customers want assurance we won't silently flip flags. offering 1:1 postmortem calls to top 3 impacted accounts.

Aj K: handing off rotation: Sanjay will be on the incident for the next 4 hours to ensure nothing regresses. I'll file a high-priority postmortem and ping legal if any contracts might be implicated.

Sanjay R: ack. will keep thread updated. removing pager at 09:45 after monitoring window.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT CLOSED (monitored): mitigations successful, error-rate stabilized. Follow-up items created in taskboard: TB-1124 (postmortem), TB-1125 (integration test), TB-1126 (migration-runbook).

Maria S: thanks team. please add any additional notes here — we'll compile the formal incident report. :pray:

Evan L: quick note — please make sure the postmortem includes the exact flag gating logic and the failing assumption about eventual index creation.

Latia M: closing CS loop: customers acknowledged and asked for timeline for repro/patch. CS will escalate if they see a regression. :white_check_mark:
